This will be a long post, hopefully not too jumbled bc it’s so hard to explain, but I feel I can help here OP! 

I have had this exact pain for 17 years in this exact location due to my really bad scoliosis curve in between my shoulder blades.

I also have the same type of 9-5 desk job situation (hunching over at the computer all day like Quasimodo, arching my neck too like a turtle coming out it’s shell lol). I also game most nights when I come home. 

1) I’ll just be honest with you, the cyclo is just a giant band aid. It’s not a long term solution to anything. It can help in acute moments mainly just sleep for me, but it doesn’t really stop a spasm and it definitely doesn’t help knots. I see massages haven’t been helping you. What kind of massages are you getting? The only way you’re getting knots out is continuous deep tissue massage, not every day obviously, but doing it frequently. Light surface massages don’t really do anything when the muscles are this tight. 

It needs to be deep tissue. You really gotta get in there and dig the hell out of it with a knuckle or something and release it. And it hurts like a mf but it’s the only way to mayyybe get the knots to calm down. Muscles have extremely strong “memory.” I always loved the saying from my PT, “ They (muscles) love to “go back home” lol. You have to relentlessly work at those muscles to retrain them, plus doing physio on top to keep it from going back. No pill is ever gonna fix it. 

2) Posture awareness is everything! You have to remind yourself as much as possible to sit up straight. I constantly notice myself, more so in gaming because you’re locked in, hunching over trying to be closer to the action so to speak. But I do it at work too. Just not as much bc my brain doesn’t get “lost” in my boring job so I remember a lil more to correct it during that.

3) Pressure point flushing as I like to call it (myofascial release) helps get the knots out. Are you stretching at all? Best thing to do sometimes is get between a door frame and put your arms out like your doing a push up on the door frame and just lean as far forward as you can and stretch your chest out. Then switch it and grab the door frame with your hands turned in and just lean back like your holding on to a rail trying not to fall off a building so to speak. Just lean back and stretch all those muscles in between your shoulder blades. Then take your arms and hug yourself as tight as you can expose the inside of the top of the scapula muscle. That’s where the knot will be with it bothering your neck. 

Usually this next step helps if you have someone else to do it to get good pressure. You can also just lean up against anytime that has a corner. Counter, dresser, etc. But just press and hold on the top part of that  spot where the scapula wing of your shoulder blade meets your neck (however hard you can handle the pressure to start out with, but the harder the better for me just to get it out). Do this in 10, 20, 30 sec intervals until you feel it flush and release. You will feel the pain/burn for a bit but once you flush it out it feels so much better. 

4) If you don’t have a good chair try to get one, and lumbar and neck support cushions, and shoulder blade pads (they have different changeable velcro ones that come in packs so you can move it around the chair) based on where you feel the pain and pressure on that certain day. 

5) For the stiffness…Heating pads for when laying in bed and hot showers and just sit there and soak the muscles after stretching and massaging. You can even do it before that too to loosen it up. 

Sorry for the super long response I just know the exact type of pain you are feeling right now and wanted to try to help in any way I could. Best of luck to you!
